extracted.intended_audience: invited nominators, potential nominees, and the general public interested in the MacArthur Fellows Program
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria used by the MacArthur Foundation to identify and choose MacArthur Fellows — highly creative individuals who will benefit from unrestricted fellowships. Describes eligibility, evidentiary materials, review process, and program expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional creativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the three explicit selection criteria. The program aims to identify extraordinarily creative individuals with a track record of excellence in a field of scholarship or area of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise for important future advances
rubrics_metrics.description: Promise for important future advances based on a track record of significant accomplishments which could be enabled by our support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection looks for individuals whose past accomplishments indicate that MacArthur support could enable important future advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for the Fellowship to facilitate subsequent creative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential for the Fellowship to facilitate subsequent creative work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of whether an unrestricted fellowship would materially enable the nominee's future creative activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record of significant achievement / excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals will have a track record of significant achievement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although fellows have significant achievements, the fellowship is not a lifetime achievement award; past accomplishments are weighed as evidence of future promise and creative capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary originality and dedication and capacity for self-direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarding unrestricted fellowships to talented individuals who have shown extraordinary originality and dedication in their creative pursuits and a marked capacity for self-direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation seeks originality, dedication to creative pursuits, and the nominee's ability to direct their own work without institutional oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to impact society through pioneering work or rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to impact society in significant and beneficial ways through their pioneering work or the rigor of their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates whose work has the potential for significant societal benefit or influence, whether through pioneering approaches or rigorous scholarship/practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in originality, insight, and potential (not lifetime achievement)
rubrics_metrics.description: While individuals will have a track record of significant achievement, the fellowship is not a lifetime achievement award—it is an investment in a person's originality, insight, and potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is placed on future-oriented potential and creative promise rather than recognition of an entire career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrestricted / no-strings-attached support (people not projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not require or expect specific products or reports from MacArthur Fellows and does not evaluate recipients' creativity during the term of the fellowship. The MacArthur Fellowship is a 'no-strings-attached' award in support of people, not projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows are not obligated to produce deliverables or reports; the fellowship's purpose is to enable creativity through flexible support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: U.S. residency/citizenship and government position restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees must be either residents or citizens of the United States and cannot hold elective office or advanced positions in government as defined by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the only formal eligibility restrictions stated on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination-only process (no applications or unsolicited nominations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees are brought to the program's attention through a constantly changing pool of invited external nominators. The Fellows Program does not accept applications or unsolicited nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only invited nominators may submit names; prospective nominees cannot apply directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bread and diversity of nominators encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominators come from as broad a range of fields and areas of interest as possible and are encouraged to draw on their expertise, accomplishments, and breadth of experience to nominate the most creative and transformative people they know within their field and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominators should consider cross-field and transformative candidates, leveraging broad expertise and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence considered in evaluation: nomination letters, external evaluations, examples of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Selectors consider each nominee with respect to the program's selection criteria and based on the nomination letter(s), numerous evaluations from subject matter experts collected by the program Staff, and examples of the nominee’s work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is evidence-based drawing on nomination letters, subject-matter expert evaluations, and concrete work samples; these are the principal inputs to selection judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent, rotating Selection Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominees are reviewed by an independent Selection Committee composed of a rotating roster of leaders in the arts, sciences, and humanities professions and in the for-profit and nonprofit communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition is multidisciplinary and rotates to bring varied perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and anonymity of nominators/evaluators/selectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominators, evaluators, and selectors all serve anonymously, and their correspondence and counsel are kept confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential/anonymous participation is intended to enable honest perspectives independent of outside influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process outcome and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: After a rigorous, multi-stage review, the Selection Committee makes its recommendations to the President and MacArthur Board of Directors. Announcement of the annual class is usually made in late September or early October. While the number of Fellows in each annual class varies, typically 20 to 30 Fellows are selected each year, representing a broad range of fields and endeavors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is multi-stage and culminates in Board approval; typical cohort sizes and announcement cadence are provided as procedural expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program aims and values to inform selection
rubrics_metrics.description: By providing these individuals with unfettered support... the Fellows Program seeks to: Highlight the importance of imaginative thinking; Spotlight the value of risk-taking in addressing deep-rooted societal problems; Expand our understanding of creativity; and Cultivate the next generation of innovators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program's explicit aims and values (imaginative thinking, risk-taking, expanding understanding of creativity, cultivating innovators) frame what kinds of creativity and impact the program prioritizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award characteristics (amount and payment schedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellowship comes with an award of $800,000 to the recipient, paid out in equal quarterly installments over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides factual context about the fellowship's scale and temporal structure which may inform expectations about the program's capacity to enable creative work.
